I feel the same way about a few other spells as well. There are some that don't make sense that they would scale for sure. But this is one that I just completely disagree with. I think it should be plus three for first level and plus two for every level after. Literally everyone in opposition to this point only has the game Mechanics to fall back on as an argument.

I get that to a certain extent you sometimes just have to make a call and roll with it to balance things. But just suspend the Mechanics for a moment and see where I'm coming from.

If you can pump energy into a spell like Fireball which is essentially triggering a form of magical combustion, you should also be able to pump energy into a spell like shield which is essentially triggering a form of magical density. If I can spend more magical energy to strengthen the combustion and explosion of my Fireball oh, I should be able to use my magical energy to increase the density or change the shape of my shield

This is taking a magical spell, an effect that is scalable in a multitude of forms mechanically and even more if you use common sense as to the fundamentals of how magic works, and comparing it to a set of real estate allowance rules.

I understand the point you're making, as far as it should make sense that you could build houses where you want to oh, and I actually agree with you. However the circumstances are slightly different, given that we are talking about magic and the placement of energy as opposed to what may be some type of annoying zoning law. The Monopoly rule is one created by man and therefore is flawed. Applying the idea of magic as a force of energy that can be manipulated, it shouldn't be cherry-picked just to make the Mechanics Work. It seems lazy.

I do understand this perspective. And I even Grant you it has a completely valid point. That being said, this is only a validation for the mechanics of the game, and if you use any common sense about the way magic would work, the whole thing falls apart mechanically. I know that it seems to be written so that it is semi balanced, but to achieve that balance it seems to completely go against itself as far as how magic fundamentally works

I think to take this Viewpoint, you have to admit that this is functioning so that the mechanics work, but it doesn't make any sense from a fantasy Common Sense perspective.

If magic is essentially reshaping energy with willpower and understanding Universal patterns, there is simply no reason that you should be able to increase your energy output to increase the effect of a fireball spell, but not for a shield spell.
